findings.problem: The focus ring token is scoped per ground - b.css:30 gives :root --focus: var(--fore) and b.css:31 gives [data-ground="paper"] --focus: var(--accent) - but .b-chat is a messaging-app plate that is hard white in BOTH rooms. On ink the ring therefore resolves to white and paints onto white. Measured on the real composite at 1440x960 and 390x844: the ring on .b-unfurl computes rgb(255,255,255) and the pixel 6px outside it is [255,255,255] on all four sides, in publish and in unfurl. Contrast 1.00:1 - the focus indicator does not exist. The same element on paper reads indigo at 6.29:1 on all four sides. On state=unfurl this is the ONLY focusable element on the screen, so an ink-room keyboard user tabbing that state gets no indicator at all; on publish it is tab stop 2 of 4, the owner's own preview of what the couple receives. Neither gate can see it: interaction-check.mjs:118 'focus paints a visible treatment' asserts only outlineWidth > 0, and audit.mjs's composited-backdrop contrast pass grades ink, not outline colour. This is the round-10 class verbatim - one token serving both grounds and surviving on only one - recurring on a different token.
findings.fix: In b.css, beside the .b-chat block, add one rule: `.b-chat { --focus: var(--accent); }`. The chat plate is a paper island in both rooms, so it must carry the paper ring. Driven verbatim at 1440x960 and 390x844 on both grounds and both states: .b-unfurl's ring becomes rgb(79,70,229) against the [255,255,255] plate (6.29:1) in the ink room, paper is unchanged, and every control outside the plate keeps its own ground's ring (paper rgb(17,17,17), ink rgb(255,255,255)) - nothing else moves.

findings.problem: Three fills in the artifact carry meaning by translucency, and a forced palette repaints all three to Canvas. Measured by sampling painted pixels at 390x844 and 1440x960 with forcedColors active, identical on paper and ink: the four .b-skel slabs paint [255,255,255] against a [255,255,255] ground (unforced they are [231,231,231] on paper and [41,41,41] on ink), so the entire content of the loading frame - the numeral block, the ceremonial date, the sub line, the sender line - disappears and the frame reduces to three text lines and the today rule; the edited row's plate paints [255,255,255] against [255,255,255] (unforced [241,241,241] / [31,31,31]), so the only visual tie between the open panel and the moment it edits is gone. The 12px box-shadow halo cannot stand in - Chromium drops box-shadow entirely in forced colours, verified by injecting a CanvasText double-shadow and scanning the column: nothing painted. The file already knows the answer and wrote it down for the tick - 'a forced palette may repaint any fill but cannot flatten a shape' - and applies it to .b-tick, the chosen segment and .b-item[data-crowded], but the @media (forced-colors: active) block never reaches these three. The gate's forced-colours passes open owner-flight only (interaction-check.mjs:2113, 3146, 3233); loading is never opened in a forced palette.
findings.fix: Inside the existing @media (forced-colors: active) block at the foot of b.css, add three rules that carry each fill as a shape in a system colour: `.b-skel { background: Canvas; border: 1px solid CanvasText; box-sizing: border-box; }`, `.b-item[data-editing="true"] .b-copy { outline: 1px solid CanvasText; outline-offset: 12px; }`, `.b-bubble { background: Canvas; border: 1px solid CanvasText; box-sizing: border-box; }`. Driven verbatim on both grounds: the four skeleton rects keep their exact boxes ([15,65,107,86], [20,161,227,26], [20,195,188,23], [20,230,92,15] at 390) and now paint a CanvasText hairline; the edited row gets a hairline at the halo's own 12px radius with documentElement.scrollHeight unchanged (2574 before and after) and no collision with the focus ring, which sits on the panel, not the row.

findings.element: .b-input - the title and WHEN fields in the editor, and the day field on owner-empty
findings.problem: b.css:1548 declares the rule in its own comment - 'Forty-four pixels is the floor for anything a thumb presses, and the file wrote that down and then applied it to one control' - then names six selectors (.b-act, .b-seg button, .b-step, .b-grab, .b-linkField, .b-undoAct) and omits the three the owner actually types into. Measured at 390x844 with hasTouch and (pointer: coarse) matching, on both grounds: the title field is 332x42, the WHEN field 332x40, and the day field on owner-empty 240x40. They are the only controls in the product below the floor the file declares, and the owner-empty field is the first thing a person who has never used the product touches - the whole plan is measured from it. The gate cannot see it: interaction-check.mjs:2098 iterates '.b-act, .b-step, .b-grab, .b-seg button' and never looks at an input.
findings.fix: Add .b-input to the existing coarse-pointer list at b.css:1552 so it reads `.b-act, .b-seg button, .b-step, .b-grab, .b-input, .b-linkField, .b-undoAct { min-height: 44px; height: auto; }`. Driven verbatim at 390x844 with touch on both grounds: the three fields go to 44px, the docked sheet is bottom-anchored so it grows upward (top 253 -> 247) while [data-act=delete]'s bottom holds at 815 and documentElement.scrollHeight is unchanged at 2644 - nothing is pushed off the sheet and no other geometry moves.

findings.problem: openEditor (render-b.js:1167) opens with `if (item.getAttribute("data-editing") === "true") return;`, but the row's badge keeps aria-expanded="true", aria-controls="b-edit" and the name 'Edit Send the invitations. Saturday 8 August, in 23 days. Shown to guests.' So the surface carries a button that announces itself as an expanded disclosure over a named panel and then answers nothing. Driven at 1440x960 and 390x844 with touch, on both grounds, with a MutationObserver over the whole body across the press: zero mutations, activeElement unchanged, scrollY unchanged, no live region written. This is not the settled count-and-tick refutation - that concerned the away figure and the tick, which are not controls and take the plain arrow cursor; this is the button itself, carrying a real ARIA state, refusing. It also strands the keyboard: the panel precedes the rows in DOM order, so from the open row the only route back to the fields it names is Shift+Tab through every preceding row. The gate's 'a press is answered' (interaction-check.mjs:1730) only counts :active CSS rules and cannot reach this.
findings.fix: In render-b.js:1167, replace the bare early return with a hand-off through the existing land(): `if (item.getAttribute("data-editing") === "true") { var open = root.querySelector("#b-edit"); if (open) land(open, root); return; }`. land() is already the one place that hands focus over without moving the page unless the target is off screen, and its declaration is hoisted above this call site. The press then does exactly what the control's own aria-controls promises - takes you to the panel it names - and the disclosure state stops being a claim the button will not honour.

biggestWin: The place-keeping is the best thing here and it holds up under real abuse. Every repaint I could provoke restores position and focus in the same frame: delete moves focus to the next row's badge with the page still at scrollY 0 and the undo bar naming what went; Ctrl+Z brings the moment back and lands focus on the restored row, not the body; Add pressed from a scrolled page opens an empty, focused field already in view; Enter in the empty state's day field commits and hands focus forward to 'Add a moment'; a refusal ('That is not a date. Try 3 October 2026.' / 'This is as far as it goes. Nothing can sit after the day itself.') keeps focus in the field that was wrong; Escape returns focus to the row that opened the editor; native undo inside a text field is untouched while Ctrl+Z outside it drives the product's own history. Resized across 1440/1280/1279/1152/768/390 the focused element keeps its identity every time. Fourteen states x two grounds with a pageerror listener attached throughout: zero page errors, zero console errors. Focus order equals visual order in the editor at both widths. Hover causes exactly zero reflow - the row halo is a box-shadow, so nothing under the cursor moves. Eight same-day moments stacked produce no .b-copy overlap at either width and the count correctly falls silent on the rows that share a mark. Reduced motion collapses every transition to 0.001s. The copy path, driven with a real clipboard grant, writes the true URL, answers on the face of the control, announces 'Link copied.' in the one live region, and restores the label after two seconds. That is Linear-grade state discipline; what remains are four edge renderings the gates cannot see, not a model problem.
